metadata.title: Šíření pryšce skvrnitého (Euphorbia maculata) na území Olomouckého a Moravskoslezského kraje
metadata.description: The paper summarises the recent distribution of Euphorbia maculata in northern Moravia and Silesia. It is an alien species originating from (sub)tropical North America. It was  likely introduced into the region in the 1940s. In the last two decades, the number of new localities of this species has increased rapidly. At present, it is known from the majority of phytochorions in the region, with the exception of mountain areas. The species is most widespread in the city of Olomouc, where it shows a tendency towards invasive behaviour. Euphorbia maculata occurs as a ruderal species and tolerates trampling. This thermophilous plant occurs in town squares, cemeteries and pebble-covered sites, among other habitats. Its spread is facilitated by the warm summer seasons of recent years.

metadata.title: Floristická překvapení v korytě otrávené řeky aneb jak Bečvě opět prospěla povodeň
metadata.description: This paper presents noteworthy floristic records of vascular plants from the riverbed of the Bečva River, one of the few remaining Czech rivers with exposed gravel deposits. During the late phase of the previous growing season, the river was strongly affected by flash floods.Several interesting species, including endangered taxa and neophytes, were recorded during 2025, almost exclusively on gravel bars. Notable findings among the endangered species included Elatine triandra, Kickxia elatine and Ranunculus sardous, all previously unrecorded from the Bečva River. Such discoveries underscore the importance of gravel deposits, which are extraordinary features of the local landscape.

metadata.title: Bryologická exkurze na Palkovické hůrky u Hukvald
metadata.description: A total of 49 mostly common bryophyte species (3 liverworts and 46 mosses) were recorded during the excursion to the Palkovické hůrky hills near the village of Hukvaldy (Moravia, Czech Republic) on September 27, 2025. Only two species are listed in the Red List under Least Concern – attention list. The moss Ptilium crista-castrensis is quite rare in the region, while Hypnum pallescens is scattered in the area of the Moravian Carpathians. Other species worth noting include Dicranoweisia cirrata, Dicranum tauricum and Syntrichia virescens. Rich populations of the invasive moss Campylopus introflexus were also found.

metadata.title: Co přinesla velká voda?
metadata.description: This report presents a brief overview of an entomological and botanical field excursion conducted along the Odra River in Ostrava on 30 August 2025, aimed at documenting post-flood conditions following the major flood of the previous year. Flood-related disturbance of riverbanks and local sediment redistribution were observed; however, channel morphology and existing regulation structures (e.g. bank reinforcements and weirs) remained largely unchanged. We observed that riparian vegetation was dominated by extensive stands of invasive alien and other competitive ruderal taxa, whereas entomological observations were limited. Post-flood mechanical clearance of the floodplain was recorded; besides anthropogenic debris, the removed material also included natural alluvial sediments, which may reduce substrate heterogeneity and early-successional habitats. In our opinion, the flood’s magnitude was insufficient to counteract the long-term effects of human river regulation, and ecological degradation persists. Overall, the persistence of channelization and transverse barriers indicates continuing constraints on habitat quality and longitudinal connectivity, potentially limiting the recovery of native biota, including the return of the migratory salmon to the Odra River system. A noteworthy finding was the presence of a large population of Salvinia natans.

metadata.title: Za přesličkami a orchidejemi na Jahodnou
metadata.description: A field trip to Jahodná hill near the city of Třinec took place on June 14, 2025. Its main destination was a large, abandoned, overgrown sludge lagoon, but some other localities were also surveyed. Several previously known species were observed on the sludge lagoon, such as Equisetum variegatum, E. ramosissimum, Epipactis atrorubens and E. palustris. Two recently discovered taxa, Equisetum ×moorei and Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani, were also confirmed, and Cephalanthera rubra has been found for the first time in the locality. In addition, nearby localities of Epipactis microphylla and Asplenium scolopendrium were visited during the field trip.

metadata.title: Ve stopách kêsanyho zeli z Bystročic
metadata.description: A botanical excursion to the intensively farmed landscape south of Olomouc was carried out on June 7, 2025. The route led from the village of Bystročice, passing newly constructed ponds with a rich assemblage of aquatic macrophytes, through long-abandoned and overgrown small limestone quarries, to the village of Nedvězí, then further to Nemilany, and finally ended in Slavonín. A total of 128 vascular plant taxa were recorded during the excursion. Among the most noteworthy species were Ranunculus rionii, Malva pusilla, Potamogeton nodosus, Brachypodium rupestre, and Carex pseudocyperus.

metadata.title: Exkurze za kontryhely (Alchemilla) Javorníků
metadata.description: A field trip focused on lady's mantles (Alchemilla) in the Javorníky Mts took place on May 31, 2025. Eight participants and two excursion leaders explored the route from the village of Malé Karlovice through Lopušná hill to Podťaté valley. Eleven Alchemilla species were successfully recorded, including A. isodonta (previously unknown from the Czech Republic), A.cymatophylla, and A. gruneica. Beyond lady's mantles, numerous orchid species and rare lichens on old ash trees were observed. The excursion demonstrated the rich biodiversity of the Javorníky Mts and confirmed that rare species can still be discovered in well-explored areas.

metadata.title: Exkurze na Filipovické louky a další půvabná místa pod Točníkem
metadata.description: The third excursion of the Moravian-Silesian Branch of the Czech Botanical Society in 2025 took place on May 24, and led to the settlement of Filipovice in the Hrubý Jeseník Mts (Silesia, Czech Republic). A range of habitats was explored, including anthropic sites, wet meadows, and mountain grasslands. The main focus was the Filipovické louky Nature Reserve, a small remnant of wet and peaty meadows with Carex flava, Dactylorhiza majalis, Eriophorum angustifolium, Valeriana dioica, and many other species. A ski slope above the settlement was the other interesting locality, where Thesium alpinum and a single plant of Dactylorhiza majalis were observed.

metadata.title: Z Balkánu Končinami skoro na Hlaváčky
metadata.description: The excursion to the surroundings of Rožnov pod Radhoštěm (Moravia, Czech Republic) took place on May 17, 2025. The route of the botanical and geological field trip led through the part of Rožnov known as Balkán, across Končiny to Rysová Mt., where it was terminated due to unfavourable weather conditions. We passed through a mosaic of meadows, fields, oak-hornbeam forests, small wetlands, and abandoned quarries preserving traces of the Tertiary Sea – menilite rock outcrops with fossil fish remains. In total, 126 taxa of vascular plants were recorded. Ononis arvensis, a species that reflects the historical use of today’s mown meadows as grazed pastures, was one of the rarer species recorded during the field trip.

metadata.title: Bryologická exkurze na pěnovcová prameniště
metadata.description: The bryological field trip took place on April 5, 2025, and led to the forests surrounding the calcareous rock Raškův kámen and the Janíkovo sedlo saddle near the village of Kopřivnice (Nový Jičín district). We surveyed calcareous forest springs with tufa formation, oak-hornbeam forest, ravine forests, forest roadsides, forest streams, and other substrates. In total, 95 bryophyte species (15 liverworts and 80 mosses) were recorded. One species, Seligeria pusilla, is classified as Vulnerable (VU) on the Czech Red List. Orthotrichum patensbelongs to the category of Lower Risk – near threatened (LR-nt). Three species, namely Didymodon tophaceus, Oxyrrhynchium speciosum, and Pedinophyllum interruptum, are classified as Least Concern – attention list (LC-att).

metadata.title: Poznámky k rozšíření některých vzácnějších druhů na Osoblažsku III
metadata.description: This paper reports on the localities of several regionally rare vascular plant species (Artemisia absinthium, Gagea minima, G. pratensis, Geranium molle subsp. molle, Hypericum humifusum, Jasione montana, Limosella aquatica, Scabiosa ochroleuca, Vicia lathyroides) in the Osoblažsko region. All were discovered at new sites in 2024. Some of these species, such as Gagea spp. and Vicia lathyroides, are likely underreported. Artemisia absinthium and Scabiosa ochroleuca were once common in this area, but are now considered very rare.

metadata.title: Bryologická exkurze za historií mechorostů v Beskydech
metadata.description: The bryological field trip took place on October 12, 2024, in the forested area around the settlement of Hlavatá and Lučovec stream near the village of Bílá (Moravskoslezské Beskydy Mts). We surveyed a variety of habitats, including a forest spring, spruce forest, fir-beech forest, the vicinities of forest roads and streams, and other substrates. In total, 78 bryophyte species (26 liverworts and 52 mosses) were recorded. Among these, Liochlaeana lanceolata and Hookeria lucens are classified as Lower Risk – Near Threatened. Four species, namely Riccardia latifrons, R. multifida, R. palmata and Trichocolea tomentella, are listed under Least Concern – Attention list.

metadata.title: Exkurze Za mechorosty na hrad Hukvaldy a jeho okolí
metadata.description: A total of 65 bryophytes taxa (7 liverworts and 58 mosses) were recorded during the excursion to Hukvaldy Castle and its surroundings on September 21, 2024. Four of these taxa are listed in the red list. Among the most noteworthy are the mosses Rhynchostegium rotundifolium and Rhynchostegiella tenella. Additionally, rich populations of the liverwort Preissia quadrata were observed in shaded corners of the castle ruins. Several other notable species, including Conocephalum conicum, Fissidens exilis, F. limbatus, Pellia endiviifolia and Syntrichia latifolia were found in the vicinity of the castle. The bryoflora of castles is the result of changes in the past and can be very interesting.

metadata.title: Za teplomilnými plevely a jiným kvítím okolo Staříča
metadata.description: On June 29, 2024, a botanical excursion took place near the village of Staříč, focusing on thermophilous weeds and other rare plants. The field trip covered diverse habitats, including mixed forests, pond shores, field margins, and fallows. Notable finds included rare weed species such as Kickxia elatine, K. spuria, Valerianella dentata, V. rimosa, and Odontites vernus subsp. vernus, among others. The excursion also included a visit to the Kamenná Nature Monument, where the occurrence of Linum flavum, L. austriacum, Gentiana lutea, and other rare thermophilous plants was confirmed.

metadata.title: Exkurze jižním okrajem CHKO Jeseníky na Přemyslovské sedlo
metadata.description: A field trip to the mountain meadows and transitional mires along the southern border of the Jeseníky PLA (N Moravia, Czech Republic) took place on June 8, 2024. The route led from the village of Rejhotice to the Přemyslovské sedlo saddle. A total of 166 vascular plant taxa were recorded during the trip. Notable finds included Cypripedium calceolus, Gymnadenia conopsea, Lilium bulbiferum, Orchis mascula subsp. speciosa, Pedicularis sylvatica, and Trifolium spadiceum.

metadata.title: Copak roste v Hnojicích?
metadata.description: The botanical excursion to the surroundings of the village of Hnojice, located in the Haná region of central Moravia, took place on June 1, 2024. The excursion explored the agricultural landscape and adjacent areas of the Litovelské Pomoraví Protected Landscape Area. Along the approximately 10 km route, we recorded several noteworthy plant species, including Thalictrum lucidum, Pseudolysimachion maritimum, Silene baccifera and the very rare and endangered Carex strigosa. The discovery of C. strigosa represents a significant range extension for this species, which had not been previously documented in the Haná region. Additionally, the excursion identified several populations of recently expanding grasses, such as Vulpia myuros and Puccinelia distans.

metadata.title: Exkurze do údolí Javorné u Zlatých Hor
metadata.description: A field trip to the Javorná valley, located in the northern corner of the Jeseníky Mts, took place on May 18, 2024. At the beginning, we surveyed ruderal and synanthropic flora in Ondřejovice. Among other species, we found Tellima grandiflora, a rarely escaping ornamental species native to North America. Later on, we passed through cattle pastures and forests west of the village, where we admired a local botanical curiosity, Cardamine chelidonia. This species, native to southern Europe, now occurs locally in the forests of the Jeseníky Mts but remains rare elsewhere in the Czech Republic. Afterwards, we reached the Javorná River valley, where we encountered another curiosity, a legally protected invasive tree (Robinia pseudoacacia, originally from North America). In total, we recorded 214 plant taxa during the field trip.

metadata.title: Cestou necestou do Podbeskydí za pampeliškami nejen sekce Taraxacum
metadata.description: On April 20, 2024, we led an excursion focused on the floristic survey of dandelions (Taraxacum) across 12 localities in the Podbeskydí region (northeastern part of the Czech Republic). In total, we recorded 54 described species of this genus, along with several other species that have not yet been scientifically identified. The majority of the species belonged to the section Taraxacum (syn.: sect. Ruderalia), although we also found representatives of the sections Hamata (T. hamatiforme) and Celtica (T. gelertii). Perhaps the most noteworthy discovery was T. cordatum (sect. Taraxacum) in the city of Třinec. This taxon had not previously been reported in the Podbeskydí region and was known from only three other localities in the Czech Republic. Additionally, we observed other notable plants accompanying the dandelions, such as Eleocharis uniglumis near the city of Frýdek-Místek.
